report.name: DecisionLog
report.title: Decision Log
report.paragraph: We will not provide handrails on the bridge as the 0.005 or 0.5% slope does not require them per ADA. Per Matt Kosar. 1.1.

Brought up the issue that conduit probably wont fit in the railing. Agreed to put 2 runs of conduit in each rail for quantities and to check with Erik Spillmann and hope the issue gets worked out later. --Per Matt Kosar 2.1.
Use 6 - 24" x5/8" Piles in the pier wall in liue of the 20" Pipe or HP's to give us more favorable FDLs and some room for conservatism -- Per Matt Kosar 3.1.
Keep the 5 - HP 14x89's for the same reason -- Per Matt Kosar 3.2.
Do not increase the pier wall thickness due to the larger 24" Pipe piles as this will effect Roadway, TCP, etc. Contractor will have to be told to be dead on 4.1.
Contractor has decided to go with a 12ft ped bridge clear width with only 2 FIB36 beams --Per Matt 5.1.
We will use one size bearing pad for all bridges on the project --Per Matt 5.2.
Moving to a Type F bearing and pedestals at 6" to facilitate 2" off leeway for camber. -- Per Matt 6.1.
report.heading: 2026-09-29 — coordinated geometry update
report.paragraph: User direction: Type F bearings, 6-in pedestals, 36-in cap depth, four 20-in piles at 6D center spacing, and 15 in from each end pile face to the cap end. Cap length is 34 ft 2 in. Use Bridge_Geo_2_Beam_Reorganized for the selected profile, slab-only area and separately counted haunch volume. This current direction supersedes the earlier pile/cap configuration; historical entries remain unchanged.
report.heading: 2026-09-29 — pile spacing corrected to 3D
report.paragraph: The user corrected pile spacing from 6D to 3D. Four 20-in piles now have three 5-ft center spaces. With 15 in from each outside pile face to the cap end, the cap length is 19 ft 2 in (3 × 60 in + 20 in + 2 × 15 in = 230 in). Cap width remains 4 ft and depth remains 36 in; cap concrete is 230 ft³ and self-weight is 34.5 kip at 150 pcf. This correction supersedes the 6D / 34-ft-2-in entry above. The pile-layout comparison now matches the retained source layout, but the changed cap section and deck dead load still require updated analysis forces.
report.heading: 2026-09-30 - Topic modules and end-bent entry
report.paragraph: Moved the former Ped Bridge sections into topic modules and updated their formula references and navigation links. Added End Bent 1 entry for the larger adjacent span: Span 1 = 107.35 ft versus Span 2 = 104.90 ft. User supplied node 12 for the bearing closer to global origin, node 19 for the other bearing, unchanged bearing spacing and a 36-in × 36-in cap. Existing pier entry load cases and calculations retain their source values.

End-bent transfer starts with centered bearing row and cap-centroid application nodes, with editable offsets. The legacy 4-ft end-bent pedestal quantity remains provisional because it exceeds the 3-ft cap width; reconcile the footprint before using its below-pad dead weight. Local deck-end concrete, direct end-bent wind and other end-bent actions remain separate as documented in the entry module.
report.heading: 2026-09-30 - Live axis and wind schematics
report.paragraph: Added independent physical-wind and coordinate-axis controls to both FBMP entry modules. Node identity and physical load state remain fixed under an axis-view change. The vertical axis is derived from the two horizontal choices to retain right-handed coordinates. All three force and moment components, node coordinates and gravity entry signs follow the view. Formula-driven arrows and a selected-case table give a visual model comparison.
report.heading: 2026-09-30 — Centered pile, eccentric bearings and upright elevations
report.paragraph: Replaced the zero end-bent bearing offset with the Bridge Geometry dimension chain. Added explicit rear-face placement and adopted beam-end clearance, separated bearing and application-node lines, and included force-transfer moments in DC, PL, DW and W1–W3. Rebuilt both Type F elevations with the beam above the pad, pedestal and cap. Retained the live right-handed model-axis controls and all unrelated modules.

section.name: EndBentResponses20261008
section.heading: 2026-10-08 — coherence responses applied
section.paragraph: This entry supersedes the open pedestal, node-number and model-currency statements in the earlier 8 October entry. Source: the user-completed End_Bent_Coherence_Review_Responses.xlsx, items 01–09; exact workbook and hash retained with T004.

01 — End-bent pedestal: 30 in along the beam, starting at the front of the 12-in backwall on a 42-in cap. Separate end-bent section inputs retain 6-in height, 42-in transverse width and 3/4-in chamfers. Quantities and local dead weights update live. Pier pedestal remains 48 in.
02 — Backwall and cheek-wall final quantities deferred by the user.

03–04 — The report contains the latest FBMP model per user. Loaded node numbers change from 12/19 to 15/34 following additional model nodes. The physical near/far identities, axes and load-transfer conventions remain the same. The different Downloads XML is not substituted.

05 — Station explanation: cap-end station = report audit station + 25 in. Bearing stations 29.50/132.49 become 54.50/157.49 in; 102.99-in spacing agrees with 103 in to displayed precision. This changes the measurement origin, not the geometry.

06 — U-bar hooks at potential pile interference may be field bent to provide clearance per user direction. Original as-drawn clash results are retained as source evidence; revised hook geometry and anchorage have not been checked in this update.

07 — Service III is not applicable to the current nonprestressed, non-post-tensioned substructure per user. Strength III, Service I and fatigue remain distinct. Original 48 pending/conditional source checks are historical, not a new recalculated count.

D-region discussion: concentrated bearing loads and pile reactions disturb ordinary beam stress distributions. The cap depth is 36 in, pile spacing is 54 in and the bearing-to-nearest-pile distance is about 24.5 in. Local load-path, nodal-zone and tie anchorage checks are separate from ordinary section moment/shear checks; this issue does not depend on prestressing. No strut-and-tie design is performed here.

08 — Both end bents follow the controlling End Bent 1 design, since their principal difference is the modest adjacent-span length difference. End Bent 1 is beside the 107.35-ft span versus 104.90 ft at the other end. No independent End Bent 2 forces are created.

09 — Removed unused FBMP Min Tip, Feet and Inches, Metric to Inches, Scratch and CAD modules and their navigation links. Their 110 stored errors are removed with those modules. Three inherited LoadCombinations reference links remain open; no numerical consumer of a removed module remains.

section.name: PierWallRings20261021
section.heading: 2026-10-21 - C017 Pier Wall, Annular Pile Rings added from the Pier Wall Design notebook (T028, T029)
section.paragraph: User direction of 21 October 2026 (run the pier wall notebook, update its calculation report and its Blockpad calculation in the journal; project decision D-071): the pier wall on welded annular pile rings is added as calculation C017 (report PierWallRings), the journal edition of the ring_wall package on its starting case. The calculation assigns the gross wall self-weight to the rings as vertical force by midplane tributaries, takes the ring moment as the pile-head compatibility moment of the rigid wall rotating on the axial and rotational springs of the pile heads with the pile group displaced by the radial placement tolerance (D-070; the former tributary-eccentricity moment is tabulated for comparison), and checks full annular contact, concrete bearing, plate bending and shear, the two continuous fillets and the adjacent ring and pipe base metal at every ring, then the minimum shrinkage and temperature steel, spacing, cover, laps and bar fit of the wall. Starting case: 2 failed checks (ring end cover and inner-grid clearance of the 23-in ring trial), no ring without full contact, 3.589 kip-in per ring against a 5.187 in kern. The project record selects the same run as PIER-WALL-TOOL, PIER-WALL-REPORT and PIER-WALL-CASE. C006 (fin plates and hairpins) stays; the choice of support concept is undecided. Native recalculation, appearance and engineering reviews not performed; no existing journal value changed; FBMP not rerun.

The user asked what the thinnest ring can be with no check above 0.95 of its limit; sweeping the plate thickness through the calculation with every other input held, the strength checks (plate bending, shear, fillets, base metal, bearing, contact) reach 0.95 of capacity only at about 0.17 in, while with the 5/16-in fillet the maximum fillet at the ring edge (leg at most the plate thickness less 1/16 in, LRFD 6.13.3.4) governs: 7/16 in is the thinnest standard plate (0.83), 3/8 in sits at 1.00, and the user chose 1/2 in. C017 is regenerated from the second 22 October 2026 starting case of the Pier Wall Design notebook (219 × 36 × 194.8625 in wall, 23 / 20.125 in rings, two 5/16-in fillets, free length to fixity 92.4 in): wall rotation 1.547e-5 rad, 5.397 kip-in per ring, largest equivalent eccentricity 1.105 in against the 5.187 in kern and all rings in full contact, as before; the largest plate bending ratio is 0.112 and the largest fillet ratio 0.081; at 1/2 in the minimum fillet of the thicker-part table is 3/16 in (1/4 in with the gap allowance), so the 5/16-in fillet reads 0.80 of the minimum and 0.71 of the ring-edge maximum; 1 failed check, the inner face-grid clearance to the 23-in ring, as before. Not changed: the CAD model (its rings of 22 October are 3/4 in thick; reconciliation pending), C006 (the support concept, fin plates or welded rings, is still undecided), the gravity sheet, C004, the FBMP exports and the pile and cap calculations. section.name: PierCheekWalls20261022
section.heading: 2026-10-22 - C018 Pier Cap Cheek Wall Design added from the Pier Cheek Wall Design notebook (T038, T039)
section.paragraph: User direction of 22 October 2026 (select the pier cap cheek wall calculation as a current project source and add it to the journal as C018; project decision D-081): the pier cap cheek walls are added as calculation C018 (report PierCheekWalls), the journal edition of the pier_cheek_wall package on its starting case (the D-059 walls and D-061 straight cap embedment of the CAD model, the C001 wind values, the C002 substructure drag coefficient and the pier cap materials). The calculation applies the LRFD 3.8.1.2.1 design wind pressure with the C001 speeds, exposure coefficient and gust factor and the 1.6 drag coefficient of C002 normal to the broad face of each wall (LRFD 3.8.1.2.3b; the full pressure governs every skew, the edge force is reported for the pier), with WS = 1.0 in Strength III, Strength V and Service I; treats the wall as a 48-in-wide cantilever from the cap top at the cap-top section and the recessed panel section; and checks flexure, minimum flexural resistance, shear, interface shear at the construction joint, crack control, the straight development of the verticals into the cap, shrinkage and temperature steel, bar spacing, clear spacing, cover and the SDM minimum thickness. Starting case: Strength III pressure 0.0600 ksf, 0.96 kip transverse and 0.24 kip longitudinal per wall, cantilever moment 1.920 kip-ft and shear 0.960 kip at the cap top; every numerical check passes (flexure 0.07 of capacity); the 12-in straight development (the LRFD 5.10.8.2.1a floor once the excess-reinforcement factor applies; 12.28 in for full yield without it) and the 2-in cover sit exactly at their limits; the shrinkage and temperature steel (0.73) carries both face requirements in the one centred mat, pending confirmation of that convention as for the end bents. The project record selects the same run as CHEEK-TOOL, CHEEK-REPORT and CHEEK-CASE. C014 (end-bent backwall and cheek walls) is unchanged. Native recalculation, appearance and engineering reviews not performed; no existing journal value changed; FBMP not rerun; selection is not engineering acceptance.

section.name: PierWallFinsWithdrawn20261022
section.heading: 2026-10-22 - C006 Pier Wall, Hairpins and Fin Plates withdrawn; calculation numbers permanent (T040)
section.paragraph: User direction of 22 October 2026 (project decision D-082): "Lets sequester the pier wall fin and hairpin calc from the project. Dont delete it but lets make it an unused unreferenced calc unless we need to revive it later" and "Lets actually give each calc a unique number so we dont have to keep renumbering them". The module C006 - Pier Wall, Hairpins and Fin Plates (report PierWallFins; the journal edition of the pier_wall_fins notebook package) is deleted from the journal; the package, its notebook, editions and committed run are kept intact under sequestered/ in the repository, removed from every build list, test, the code-excerpt library and the design atlas, and can be revived by the steps in sequestered/README.md. The project carries the welded annular-ring support concept: C017 Pier Wall, Annular Pile Rings, matching the CAD model rings of D-076 and D-079; this withdrawal is a scope decision, not an engineering acceptance of C017, whose grid-clearance failure and five scope items keep their recorded status. Calculation numbers are permanent identifiers: a withdrawn calculation keeps its number and the number is never reused (C005 and C006 are retired), no module is renumbered, and a new calculation takes the next unused number after C018. C017 is regenerated from its unchanged starting case with identical definitions, caches and figures; its hidden working notes and the "Outside this calculation" sentence now record the withdrawal instead of an undecided support concept. The index entry of C006 is removed; the "Calculations C001 to C018" heading, the stylerules of C006, the gravity sheet, C004 and C002 are unchanged. Native recalculation, appearance and engineering reviews not performed; no engineering value changed.
